rationale: X produced no review at all (harness crashed with a 402 API error before the review step ran), so it has zero recall, precision, and actionability. Y is a thorough, well-grounded review with specific file:line citations and concrete repros (e.g. unvalidated max_seqlen_q/k, all-False mask launching a zero-token kernel), but it misses the two substantive ground-truth findings: it doesn't catch the SAGE-disabling duplicate-boundary bug (P2) and in fact praises the trimming logic that GT says is incomplete, and its AllGather-KV discussion (finding #6) appears to reference code/fix state not present in the reviewed diff, making it only tangentially related to P1 rather than a direct catch. Y is still far more useful than X's total failure, so the win for Y is decisive despite modest recall.
